claim: For the standard five-simplex \(\Delta_5=\{x\in\mathbb R^5:x_j\ge0,\sum_{j=1}^5x_j\le1\}\), let \(F(k)=\int_{\Delta_5}e^{-2\pi i\langle k,x\rangle}\,dx\) for \(k\in\mathbb Z^5\), and let \(\Lambda(k)=\{0,k_1,\ldots,k_5\}\) be a multiset. Then \(F(k)=0\) exactly when all six nodes are distinct, or, after an integer translation normalizing the minimum to zero, \(\Lambda=\{0,0,p,p+q,p+q,p+q+r\}\) with \(qr=p(p+q+r)\), or \(\Lambda=\{0,p,p,p+q,p+q+r,p+q+r\}\) with \(pq=r(p+q+r)\), where \(p,q,r\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.domain: The standard five-simplex \(\Delta_5\) with Lebesgue measure and integer frequencies \(k\in\mathbb Z^5\) under the stated Fourier convention.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: The proof is explicit residue/divided-difference algebra. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
limitations: No classification is claimed for noninteger real or complex frequencies.
The literature search is bounded and does not establish global novelty by absence of results.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Complete classification of integer-frequency zeros, including all repeated-node multiplicity patterns for \(k\in\mathbb Z^5\).

title: Exact lattice-zero classification for the standard five-simplex \(\Delta_5\)
